title: Government
description: Jordan is governed as a constitutional monarchy. The system of government shapes daily life through laws, services, and the citizen's relationship to the state. Its modern form dates to 1946 (independence) — and like all governments, it continues to evolve with its people.

title: Independence and statehood
description: Statehood in Jordan: 1946 (independence). National days, flags, and anthems all trace to the moment of independence or founding — the story every schoolchild learns. Understanding it explains the country's pride, its holidays, and often its friendships and rivalries.

title: Languages
description: Language in Jordan: Arabic. Language carries the culture's humor, proverbs, and worldview — learning even greetings opens doors that stay closed to outsiders. Multilingual countries code-switch daily; visitors who try the local tongue are repaid with warmth.

title: Currency and money
description: Money in Jordan: the Jordanian dinar. Travelers should learn the denominations, the tipping customs, and whether cards or cash rule daily life. Exchange rates move, but the habit of checking prices in local terms keeps budgets honest.
